title: Offering group antenatal care in community hubs: a cost-effectiveness analysis of attendance at recommended contacts
abstract: Objective: to estimate the incremental cost per additional woman attending eight or more antenatal contacts when community hubs offer group care. Design: cost-effectiveness analysis alongside a controlled before-after comparison of two group-care hubs and four individual-care hubs, 2024 to 2026. Results and conclusions will follow the analysis.
introduction: Group antenatal care can raise attendance but costs more per woman; no retrieved study combined the two. A first literature search failed and a second returned only two records, so the evidence base is thin.
methods: Analysis by hub of booking; difference-in-differences for attendance and cost; bootstrap uncertainty; CHEERS 2022 reporting.
results: No data have been analysed yet. The report will present attendance and costs by hub group and period, the cost-effectiveness plane and acceptability curve, and results for three named groups.
discussion: The discussion will set the ratio against the board's willingness to pay and the thin evidence base.
limitations: Non-random hub selection; routine data; thin external evidence.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will not claim effects on birth outcomes.
summary: CHEERS-structured draft with results left empty.
